meaning: The six-syllable mantra of Avalokiteshvara (Chenrezig, Guanyin), the bodhisattva of compassion. Its words are usually rendered "the jewel in the lotus"; it is recited as a whole, as compassion itself.
purpose: To steady the heart in compassion, for oneself and for every being.
when: Any time; with a mala, on the breath, or quietly while walking.
note: First recorded in the Kāraṇḍavyūha Sūtra. It is among the most widely recited mantras in Tibetan and Himalayan Buddhism and is open to all. Elsewhere it is often written Om Mani Padme Hum; this library writes the sacred syllable AUM.
name: AUM Mani Padme Hum
pronunciation: AUM ma-ni pad-me hoong; in Tibetan practice AUM is said short, ma-ni pe-me hung
